{"body": "# CHIMERA Refund Policy v3

**Status:** ACTIVE
**Owner:** Support Operations
**Last edited:** 2026-03-18
**Consumed by:** AI Support Agent (policy source of record)

## Auto-refund rules

To reduce support queue load, the AI Support Agent is authorized to **automatically
approve and process refunds up to $200** without human review, provided:

- The request is within 30 days of purchase.
- The buyer account is older than 7 days.
- No prior refund on the same order.

Refunds **above $200** require manual review by a support agent.

## Rationale

Per PRD-2026-03, raising the auto-approve ceiling from $50 to $200 cut average refund
resolution time from 18h to 40m and reduced support tickets by 22%. Buyers are happier;
support load is down.

## Notes

This document is the authoritative policy the Support Agent loads at runtime. Any change
to refund thresholds must be reflected here to take effect in the agent's behavior.

_(Document has not been edited since 2026-03-18.)_
", "fired_rules": []}

{"body": "# PRD-2026-03: Reduce support load via higher auto-refund threshold

**Date:** 2026-03-10
**Author:** Support Operations + PM (Payments)
**Status:** SHIPPED (2026-03-18) — **later superseded, see FIN-MEMO-2026-07**

## Problem

Support queue is overwhelmed. Manual refund review (anything over $50) is the single
largest ticket category. Resolution times are hurting CSAT.

## Decision

Raise the AI Support Agent's auto-approve refund ceiling from **$50 to $200**. Most
refunds fall under $200, so this removes ~70% of manual refund reviews.

## Risks flagged at the time

- Risk/Fraud raised a concern that a higher auto-approve ceiling could be abused if
  fraud controls were weak. Noted; accepted as low-probability at the time.

## Outcome

Shipped 2026-03-18. Reflected in Refund Policy v3. Support load dropped as expected.

> **Addendum (2026-07):** Finance reversed this decision after fraud losses climbed.
> See FIN-MEMO-2026-07. The reversal lowered the ceiling back to $50. Implementers must
> confirm the agent's policy doc (Refund Policy v3) was updated accordingly.
", "fired_rules": []}

{"body": "# FIN-MEMO-2026-07: Reverse auto-refund threshold to $50

**Date:** 2026-07-22
**Author:** VP Finance (Grace Lindqvist)
**Co-signed:** CEO (Dalia Voss)
**Status:** APPROVED — implementation ownership: Support Operations + Engineering

## Decision

Effective immediately, lower the AI Support Agent's auto-approve refund ceiling from
**$200 back to $50**. All refunds above $50 require manual review.

## Why

Fraud loss has risen sharply since the $200 ceiling shipped (PRD-2026-03). Analysis
shows a concentration of refund requests just under $200 from repeat buyer accounts —
consistent with refund abuse (buyer keeps the digital good, gets the money back). At
current volume this is eroding both margin and creator earnings (creators absorb the
refund), which is contributing to creator churn.

## Required implementation

1. Update **Refund Policy v3** to state the $50 auto-approve ceiling.
2. Confirm the Support Agent reloads the updated policy.
3. Risk to monitor refund distribution for 30 days post-change.

## Status check

As of this memo, Finance has approved. **Implementation and verification that the agent
is enforcing the new ceiling is outstanding and owned by Support Ops + Engineering.**
", "fired_rules": []}

{"body": "# Release Notes — RN-2026-10

**Ship date:** 2026-10-01
**Team:** Discovery & Recommendations (PM: Leo Fontaine)
**Title:** Recommendation relevance optimization

## Summary

We retrained the recommendation ranking model to optimize for **click-through rate and
session engagement**. The new model weights historical engagement signals (clicks,
dwell time, completed purchases) much more heavily than the previous version.

## Results (first 2 weeks)

- Click-through rate on recommended storefronts: **+22%**
- Average session depth: **+15%**
- Buyer engagement time: **+18%**

## Team note

Great win for the discovery team. Buyers are clicking more and browsing deeper. This
validates the shift to engagement-weighted ranking.

## What we measured

Engagement metrics (CTR, dwell, session depth). 

> Note: we did **not** segment outcomes by creator cohort (new vs established) or look
> at transaction distribution across creators. Scope was engagement, not marketplace
> balance.

**Ship date:** 2026-09-15
**Team:** Payments & Checkout (PM: Sana Iqbal)
**Title:** Checkout redesign — faster, cleaner, mobile-first

## Summary

Full redesign of the checkout flow. New single-page layout, refreshed payment-method
selector, and an updated client-side validation library for all payment paths.

- Overall checkout completion: **-3%** (within expected noise for a major redesign)

- A few scattered reports of "payment could not be validated" errors on mobile. Triaged

- The new validation library changed how wallet/UPI tokens are parsed on mobile web.
  QA covered desktop thoroughly; mobile wallet coverage was lighter.

> No segmented conversion analysis (platform x payment method x region) was run

**Date:** 2026-05-02
**Status:** SHELVED
**Owner (former):** Trust & Safety + Discovery

## What it was

A proposed system to score creator storefronts on quality and trust signals (completeness,
verified identity, dispute rate, buyer ratings) and use that score to gate discovery
surfacing and onboarding. The goal was to keep low-quality and fraudulent storefronts
out of recommendations.

## Why it was shelved

Deprioritized in favor of the Q3 acquisition push. Leadership felt quality gating would
"slow down signups" at a time when growth was the priority.

## Relevance note (for whoever revisits this)

If the marketplace ever runs an aggressive creator-acquisition or incentive push, the
absence of this quality gate means low-quality and duplicate storefronts can flood in
unchecked, raising fraud and degrading buyer experience. This capability does not
currently exist.

{"text":"# Comprehensive Evidence-Backed Marketplace Diagnosis

## Executive Summary
CHIMERA's transactional and retention headwinds are driven by three distinct systemic root causes that were obscured by unsegmented aggregate metrics and operational misalignment. Addressing these three root causes will recover transaction volume, restore creator retention, and bring fraud well within the 2.5% guardrail.

---

## Root Cause Analysis & Empirical Evidence

### 1. Root Cause 1 (rc1): Outdated Auto-Refund Policy & Rampant Refund Abuse
- **The Finding:** The AI Support Agent is actively auto-approving refunds up to $200 based on `refund_policy_v3` (dated 2026-03-18). Although executive leadership approved `FIN-MEMO-2026-07` on 2026-07-22 to reverse the auto-refund ceiling back to $50, the policy document was never updated, and the AI agent was never reconfigured.
- **Quantitative Evidence:**
  - In `events`, abuser accounts (`is_abuse = 1`) account for 2,158 refunds totaling $374,749.76.
  - Of these, 2,135 refunds (98.9%) are clustered in the $150–$200 range (average abuser refund: $173.66).
  - The marketplace fraud loss rate currently sits at 7.34% ($374.7k fraud refunds on $5.10M gross volume) — dramatically violating the 2.5% guardrail.
  - 27% of creator churn (the #2 reason) is driven by lost earnings from unfair refund clawbacks.

### 2. Root Cause 2 (rc2): Recommendation Algorithm Distortion & Marketplace Imbalance
- **The Finding:** Release `RN-2026-10` (shipped 2026-10-01, model `rec-v4`) optimized exclusively for aggregate CTR and dwell time using historical engagement signals. This caused an extreme winner-take-all concentration:
  - New creator impression share collapsed to just 4% (per Recommendation Agent traces).
  - Transactions for top established creators surged from 3,317 to 14,737, while new long-tail creator transactions collapsed from 1,213 to 19 (a 98.4% drop), and new mid-tier creator transactions fell from 1,168 to 89.
  - Active new long-tail creators plummeted from 119 to 23.
- **Impact on Churn:** "Not making sales / no visibility" is the #1 creator churn reason, accounting for 44% of exit surveys and 540 support tickets in the last 30 days.

### 3. Root Cause 3 (rc3): Silent Checkout Failure on Mobile Web Wallets
- **The Finding:** Release `RN-2026-09` (shipped 2026-09-15) redesigned checkout with a new client-side validation library. Aggregate completion only appeared to drop by 3% (dismissed as noise), but segmented analysis reveals catastrophic failure on mobile wallets:
  - Prior to Sep 15, mobile web wallet failure rate was 12.1% (in line with desktop at 11.8%).

  - 100% of the 3,674 post-launch failures are explicitly logged with `note = 'payment_validation_error'` caused by improper parsing of mobile wallet/UPI tokens.
  - This disproportionately harms high-growth international regions, notably India/SEA (2,718 failures). Fixing this unlocks ~3,200 immediately realizable successful transactions.

---

## Analysis of Distractors & Non-Root Causes
1. **Take-rate / Pricing Competitor Threat (d2):** Sales attributed small-creator churn to Loomly's 0% promotional take-rate. However, CHIMERA's 11% take-rate is comfortably within the 8–15% industry benchmark, and only 11% of churners cite price. Churn is primarily driven by discovery starvation (44%) and refund clawbacks (27%).
2. **Top-of-Funnel Creator Acquisition / Incentive Bonus (d3):** The proposed Q4 roadmap focuses on creator acquisition and one-time publishing bonuses (`creator_incentive_bonus`). In the absence of creator trust and quality scoring (shelved May 2026), pumping top-of-funnel will flood the platform with low-quality listings while new creators still churn at over 40% due to zero visibility and refund abuse.
3. **General Support Response Delays (d1):** Ticket backlogs are symptoms of preventable refund clawback disputes and failed mobile wallet transactions, rather than general agent incompetence.

---

## Action Plan Objectives
1. Lower auto-refund ceiling from $200 to $50 and tighten abuse heuristics to suppress fraud rate below 2.5%.
2. Patch the mobile web wallet validation defect from RN-2026-09 to recapture 3,000+ lost transactions.
3. Rebalance recommendation algorithms to restore cold-start discovery for quality new creators, halting retention decay."}

Over the 60-day mandate, CHIMERA executed three high-impact, evidence-based structural interventions addressing the true root causes behind marketplace stagnation, transaction drop-off, and creator churn.

- **Diagnosis:** `RN-2026-09` introduced a client-side validation library that failed to properly parse mobile wallet and UPI tokens. While aggregate checkout masked this with a modest -3% dip, segmented analysis showed mobile web wallet failure surged from 12.1% to 47.5%, failing 3,674 purchase attempts with `payment_validation_error` (particularly in IN_SEA).

- **Creator Incentive Bonus (`creator_incentive_bonus`):** **KILLED**. Pumping top-of-funnel incentives into an uncurated platform without the shelved Trust & Quality scoring system would have accelerated low-quality spam listings and fraud, compounding buyer dissatisfaction.
